generatedProse.concept-context: In sport and exercise science, working with the whole cycle might begin with a practical module built around coaching sessions you run yourself. You read its criteria and see they reward safe, well-planned practice and clear reflection, so you aim your session plan there. When feedback flags your planning, you carry that into the next session.
generatedProse.worked-example: A sport student gets a coaching assignment back with the comment that his session plan is vague on progression. He could just read the grade and move on. Instead he checks the criteria, sees that clear progression is what the top band rewards, and plans to build it in next time. His next plan works with the whole cycle, and his marks climb.
generatedProse.summary: In sport and exercise science, how a module is designed, what its criteria reward, and the feedback you get all aim at the same practical skills. Read them as one picture and each assignment can target the same outcomes. The connected habit is what improves your work across the course.

check.body: A student reads how a module is designed, checks the marking criteria before writing, and uses the feedback on each essay to plan the next. Over the term her work improves. What does this show?

items.text: Their next round of learning and preparation, which is why the following programme improved.
Nothing; feedback comes at the end, so it cannot affect anything that follows.
Only the mark on the first programme, which cannot now change.
The deadline for the next programme.

feedback.correct: That's right. Using the feedback fed back into the next round of learning and preparation, which is why the following programme improved: that is the cycle working.
feedback.incorrectNotFinal: Not quite. Think about what the student changed before the next programme, not the old mark or the deadline.
feedback.incorrectFinal: Using the feedback fed back into the student's next round of learning and preparation, which is why the next programme improved. The old mark cannot change and the deadline is not part of the cycle; feedback is not the end, it feeds the next turn.

_items.text: That working with the whole cycle pays off: reading the design, the criteria and the feedback together kept each piece aimed at the same outcomes.
_items.feedback: Yes. She treated the three parts as one connected cycle, and each piece built on the last.

_items.text: That only the marking criteria matter, and the rest can be ignored.
_items.feedback: She used all three parts, not the criteria alone. Together they kept her work on target.

_items.text: That her tutor marked the later essays more generously.
_items.feedback: The point is not the marking. Her work improved because she worked with the whole cycle.

_items.text: That feedback is useful only at the end of a module.
_items.feedback: She used feedback after each essay, to shape the next. That is the cycle turning.
